title: Toil and Technology
candidate_claim: A retrospective account says ATMs shifted teller tasks rather than mechanically determining teller employment.
notes: Discovery context only; grade against underlying research where possible.

title: Computer and Internet Use in the United States: 1984 to 2009
candidate_claim: US Census tables document computer-use series spanning 1984–2009.
notes: Documents diffusion context; it does not establish workplace causality.

title: Growth trends for selected occupations considered at risk from automation
candidate_claim: BLS documents large historical employment declines in selected occupations while warning that causes can be confounded.
notes: Use its attribution cautions, not a simple automation story.

title: The Skill Content of Recent Technological Change: An Empirical Exploration
candidate_claim: US research links computerization with changes in task demand between 1960 and 1998.
notes: A task-demand study, not a forecast or a universal mechanism.

title: Computerization of White Collar Jobs
candidate_claim: For US office and administrative support postings, software adoption coincided with higher stated skill requirements and task broadening.
notes: Posting and local-labour-market evidence; bounded to the study period and setting.

title: How Computer Automation Affects Occupations: Technology, Jobs, and Skills
candidate_claim: A research paper uses ATMs to illustrate that task automation may coincide with organisational expansion and changed jobs.
notes: Use as a counter-example, not proof that automation preserves jobs.

title: Robots and Jobs: Evidence from US Labor Markets
candidate_claim: Industrial-robot exposure between 1990 and 2007 was associated with lower employment and wages in US commuting zones.
notes: Local-market estimates; not a claim about every firm, worker, or technology.
